analysis.evidence: שָׂפָה אֶחָת וּדְבָרִים אֲחָדִים describes the condition of כָל הָאָרֶץ at the opening of the narrative. The whole earth had one language and the same words.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces the Qal wayyiqtol יְהִי, third person masculine singular.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: כָל הָאָרֶץ means “the whole earth.” The shared language, שָׂפָה אֶחָת, shows that the phrase refers collectively to the earth’s inhabitants.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: כָל הָאָרֶץ means “the whole earth.” The description שָׂפָה אֶחָת, “one language,” shows that the earth stands for the people who inhabit it.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. Its initial א takes qamats in the definite form.

analysis.evidence: שָׂפָה אֶחָת means “one language.” The subject כָל הָאָרֶץ extends this description to all the earth’s inhabitants, and וּדְבָרִים אֲחָדִים describes the words they shared.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix. The numeral אֶחָת agrees with it in gender and number.

analysis.evidence: In שָׂפָה אֶחָת, the numeral describes the language shared by כָל הָאָרֶץ, the whole earth. Everyone spoke the same language.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral modifying the feminine singular noun שָׂפָה.
analysis.sense: one and the same; made one, united
